The second surah is the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he. His wealth will not avail him, nor what he earned. He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, around her neck a rope of fiber.﴾ [al-Masad 1-5].

Subhan Allah! This Qur'an contains such numerous proofs that clearly indicate that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is truthful, that he does not call for kingship, nor for status, nor for leadership of his people at all. The Messenger's paternal uncles (may the prayers and peace of Allah be upon him) divided, in their dealing with him and their dealing with his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, into three categories: a category that believed in him, strove alongside him, and submitted to Allah, Lord of the worlds; a category that supported and assisted him but remained upon disbelief, and we seek refuge in Allah; and a category that opposed and obstructed him, and they were disbelievers.

As for the first, they are al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, and the second is better than the first, because the second is among the most excellent of martyrs in the sight of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. "The Prophet (ﷺ) described him as the Lion of Allah and the Lion of His Messenger."[[Al-Tabarani narrated in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2952) with his chain from the hadith of Lubaybah al-Ashhaliyyah (may Allah be pleased with her) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By the One in whose hand is my soul, it is written with Allah in the seventh heaven: Hamzah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, the Lion of Allah and the Lion of His Messenger."]] He was martyred at Uhud, may Allah be pleased with him, in the third year after the Hijrah; may Allah gather me and you with him in the Gardens of Bliss.

As for the one who supported and assisted while remaining upon disbelief, he is Abu Talib. Abu Talib stood with the Prophet ﷺ in the finest stand in defending him and supporting him, but he, and we seek refuge in Allah, had already been preceded by the decree of punishment; he did not embrace Islam. Even "at the end of his life, at the last moment of the world, the Prophet ﷺ offered him that he embrace Islam, but he refused, and indeed he died upon his saying: he is upon the religion of 'Abd al-Muttalib."[[Al-Bukhari (1360) and Muslim, and the wording is his (24 / 39), with their two chains from the hadith of al-Musayyab ibn Hazn (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: When Abu Talib's death approached, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came to him and found with him Abu Jahl and 'Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O uncle, say: There is no god but Allah, a word by which I may testify for you before Allah." Abu Jahl and 'Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah said: O Abu Talib, will you turn away from the religion of 'Abd al-Muttalib?! The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept offering it to him and repeating that statement to him, until Abu Talib said, as the last thing he spoke to them: He is upon the religion of 'Abd al-Muttalib. And he refused to say: There is no god but Allah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Allah, I will surely seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from you." So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿It is not for the Prophet and those who believe to seek forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Tawbah: 113]. And Allah the Exalted revealed concerning Abu Talib, saying to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: ﴿Indeed, you guide not whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills, and He is most knowing of the guided﴾ [al-Qasas: 56].]], "so the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, interceded for him until he was in a shallow fire, and upon him were two sandals whose heat boils his brain."[[Al-Bukhari (3883) and Muslim, and the wording is his (209 / 375), with their two chains from the hadith of al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib (may Allah be pleased with him), who said to the Prophet ﷺ: What did you avail your uncle? For he used to protect you and become angry for your sake. He said: "He is in a shallow fire, and had it not been for me, he would be in the lowest level of the Fire."]].

As for the third, who opposed and obstructed, he is Abu Lahab. Allah revealed concerning him a complete surah that is recited in the prayers, obligatory and voluntary, in private and in public; a person is rewarded for reciting it at ten good deeds for every letter. That is, whoever reads the biography of Abu Lahab contained in this surah receives ten good deeds for every letter. But if you read the biography of Abu Bakr from the Sirah of Ibn Ishaq, or from al-Bidayah wa al-Nihayah and others, you would not obtain this reward. So a person is, as it were, strongly invited to read the biography of Abu Lahab; every letter you read from "Tabbat" earns you ten good deeds.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾, and this is a response to his statement—that is, the statement of Abu Lahab—"when the Prophet ﷺ gathered them to call them to Allah, giving glad tidings and warning, Abu Lahab said: Perish you! Is it for this that you gathered us?!"[[Agreed upon; narrated by al-Bukhari (4801) and Muslim in similar wording (208 / 355) from the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with both of them).]] This expression is for belittling: that is, this is a trivial matter that does not require the leaders of Quraysh to be gathered for it. This is like their saying: ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾ [al-Anbya' 36], meaning: who disparages and reviles them—that is, the Messenger. Quraysh says: ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾; the meaning is belittlement: he is nothing, does not deserve it, and is not to be concerned with. As they said: ﴿And they said: Why was this Qur'an not sent down to a great man of the two cities?﴾ [al-Zukhruf 31].

The upshot is that Abu Lahab said: Perish you! Is it for this that you gathered us?! So Allah responded to him with this surah: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he﴾. Al-Tabbab is ruin, as the Exalted said: ﴿And the scheme of Pharaoh is nothing but in ruin﴾ [Ghafir 37], that is, loss. He began with the two hands before the self because the two hands are the instruments of work, movement, taking and giving, and the like.

This title (Abu Lahab) is wholly suitable to his state and his end. The aspect of suitability is that this man will be in a Fire that blazes, we seek refuge in Allah, flaming with a great blaze; so his kunyah (agnomen) corresponds to his state and his end. A poet says:

Rarely have your eyes seen a bearer of a title ∗∗∗ except that its meaning—if you reflect—fits its bearer.

"When Suhayl ibn 'Amr came in the account of the Battle of Hudaybiyah, the Messenger ﷺ said: 'This is Suhayl ibn 'Amr, and I think he will make your affair easy for you.'"[[Al-Bukhari (2731) with his chain from al-Miswar ibn Makhramah: The Prophet ﷺ said: "This is Mikraz, and he is a wicked man." He began speaking with the Prophet ﷺ, and while he was speaking to him, Suhayl ibn 'Amr came. Ma'mar said: Ayyub informed me from 'Ikrimah that when Suhayl ibn 'Amr came, the Prophet ﷺ said: "Your affair has been made easy for you."]]; because the name corresponds to the action.

Ibn 'Uthaymin said, may Allah have mercy on him, regarding the verse:

The Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he. His wealth will not avail him, nor what he earned.﴾ The word ﴿مَا (mā)﴾ here may be interrogative, meaning: "What benefit did his wealth and what he earned bring him?" What? The answer: nothing. It may also be a negation, meaning: his wealth and what he earned did not avail him anything. Both meanings are interrelated, and their sense is that his wealth and what he earned did not avail him at all, even though it is customary that wealth is beneficial. A person can ransom himself with wealth: if an enemy overpowered him and said, "I will give you such-and-such amount of wealth and release me," he would be released. Yet the enemy may ask for much or little wealth. If he fell ill, he would benefit from his wealth; if he were hungry, he would benefit from his wealth. So wealth does benefit, but the benefit that does not save its owner from the Fire is not really benefit. For this reason He said: ﴿His wealth will not avail him﴾, meaning: against Allah, in any way.

As for His words ﴿nor what he earned﴾, it has been said that the meaning is: what he earned of children. It is as if He said: his wealth and his children did not avail him, like the statement of Nuh: ﴿And they followed those whom neither their wealth nor their children increased except in loss﴾ [Nuh 21]. Those who take this view interpret His words ﴿what he earned﴾ as referring to children, and they support this view with the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Indeed the best of what you eat is from your earnings, and indeed your children are from your earnings."[[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi (1358) from the hadith of 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.]] The correct view, however, is that the verse is more general than this: it includes children, and it includes wealth earned that is no longer in his hand, and it includes what he earned of honor and standing. Whatever he earned that increased his nobility and dignity, it will not avail him anything: ﴿His wealth will not avail him, nor what he earned﴾.

The Qur'anic verse (3) is in ﴿ ﴾ markers. Translating.

**Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 111, verse 3:**

﴿He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame﴾. The sīn (س) in his saying ﴿He will burn﴾ is for near future, which confirms the event and brings it close; meaning that Allah, the Exalted, promised him, or threatened him, that he will burn in a Fire of blazing flame. I told you: the sīn is for confirmation and nearness; meaning that he will burn, in the near future, in a Fire of blazing flame. This is because staying in this world, however long it lasts, the Hereafter is near. Even the people in the barzakh (the intermediate state between death and resurrection), although millions of years pass over them, it is as if it were an hour: ﴿As if they had not remained but an hour of a day. A proclamation. Then will any be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾ [al-Ahqaf 35]. And something that is measured as an hour of a day, I think we agree that it is near and nothing.

He, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame (3) and his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾ (...) This sīn confirms and brings near, so his burning in the Fire of blazing flame is a certain and near matter.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 111, verse 4:

﴿He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame﴾ [Qur'an 111:3]. And likewise his wife with him, ﴿and his wife, the carrier of firewood﴾. Meaning: likewise his wife with him, may Allah protect us. She was a woman from the nobility of Quraysh, but her nobility did not avail her anything, because she shared with her husband in transgression, sin, and persistence in disbelief.

As for His saying, ﴿the carrier of firewood﴾, it has been recited with both the accusative (naṣb) and the nominative (raf'). As for the accusative, it may be a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) of "woman": meaning, "and his wife, in the state of being a carrier of firewood." Or it may be in the accusative by way of censure (dhamm), since a qualifier that has been separated (from its governing noun) may be put in the accusative for censure; that is, "I censure the carrier of firewood." As for the reading with the nominative, it is an attribute (ṣifah) of "woman."

﴿The carrier of firewood﴾: what is the firewood that she carries and bears in large quantity? That is, is ﴿carrier﴾ (ḥammālah) an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālaghah)?

They mention that she would carry thorny firewood and place it on the path of the Prophet ﷺ, may Allah protect us, in order to harm the Messenger ﷺ.

Its verse: "Around her neck is a rope of palm fiber." Al-jid: the neck; al-habl: the rope, which is well known; al-masad: fiber. The meaning is that she wears a rope of fiber around her neck, with which she goes out into the desert to tie up the firewood she brings to place in the path of the Prophet (ﷺ). We seek refuge with Allah from that. This is an indication of the lowliness of her standing and that she debased herself: a woman of Quraysh, one of the most prominent clans of Quraysh, goes out into the desert and places this rope of fiber around her neck, despite the humiliation in it, but for the sake of harming the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him. We ask Allah for well-being.

With this, the discussion concluded, by what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, facilitated for us regarding these two surahs.
